newsitem.title: USA: FCC chief sees no cut in rural phone subsidies.
newsitem.headline: FCC chief sees no cut in rural phone subsidies.

text.p: The head of the Federal Communications Commission said Wednesday it was unlikely the FCC would over the next three years cut the $1.1 billion in subsidies now flowing to small and rural phone companies.
Regulators are overhauling the multi-billion dollar system for subsidising phone service in high-cost rural areas and low-income neighbourhoods. Work is set to be done in early May.

But FCC Chairman Reed Hundt said regulators are postponing any steps that could affect rural and small carriers, because the issue requires further study. "It's too early to address this issue," Hundt told a Senate Commerce Committee hearing.
Eight percent of the nation's phone lines are served by small and rural carriers.

Anxious rural lawmakers fear that changes in the support system known as universal service could result in subsidies to their areas being slashed, a move that could result in a jump in the price of rural phone service.

"It would be grossly negligent for the FCC to act in a piecemeal way which significantly reduces universal service subsidies and leaves states with the dilemma of raising local rates or allowing service to deteriorate," Sen. Conrad Burns, R-Montana, said at the hearing.
"Such an outcome would be totally unacceptable."

But Hundt told the hearing "I don't believe the FCC will take steps in the foreseeable future" to reduce the existing $1.1 billion in support to small and rural phone carriers. He later specified the time frame as over the next three years.
